34: And they are not experts to the public, etc. — The Sma wrote that the Rambam holds that even a [single] mumcheh, and even two mumchim [do not make an admission before them binding], and this is what the Mechaber concludes when he writes "even if they are ordained," for whoever is ordained is presumably a mumcheh; and it is astonishing regarding the Rama that he mixed the two opinions together and did not write them in the language of a dispute as the Tur did; and one can answer, with difficulty, that what the Rama wrote "mumcheh la'rabim" means that the public appointed them over themselves, for in such a case it helps — end of the Sma's words. But this is not illuminating, for what does it matter that the public appointed them over themselves — they are still not a beis din; and also the language does not imply so; and further, from where did he derive this din? Rather, certainly the Rav's (Rama's) intent is according to its plain sense, and the reason he did not write it in the language of a dispute is because, since in the Mechaber's own language there is not so much of a proof — for one can say [the Mechaber means] semuchim who are not mumchim (since the Rosh and Tur hold below in siman 25 that semichus helps even for one who is not a mumcheh — see there in seif katan 22 — and so it is implied in the Ir Shushan, who wrote that two, even if ordained, their ruling is not a valid ruling, and immediately after wrote that a single mumcheh may judge against [the litigant's] will) — whereas in the Rambam's own language that the Tur brings it is explicitly stated "even a mumcheh," see there — therefore the Tur wrote it in the language of a dispute, and so is the way of the Rama in many places, and this is clear. And regarding the law: what the Tur wrote, that from the words of the Rosh it appears there is no distinction between a single mumcheh and three hedyotos for any matter — in my humble opinion this is not so, for the Rosh equated a single mumcheh with three hedyotos only regarding judging, not regarding admission; and it appears primary like the Rambam and the Mechaber. And so wrote the Baal HaTerumos, sha'ar 42, chelek 1, in the name of a responsum of the early authorities, and the Tur brings it below in siman 81 se'if 27; and so appears the view of the Ir Shushan, who omitted here what the Rama glossed, "and they are not mumchim," etc. And so wrote the Baal HaIttur, in the section on admission, daf 105 amud alef, in this language: "and these matters are before three, but before a single mumcheh his admission is not [a binding] admission," end quote. And so is implied also in the second perek of Kesubos (daf 22 amud alef) and in perek Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin daf 30 amud alef), regarding kiyum and odisa, concerning "and Ravna Ashi said to us," according to the girsa of the Rif and the Rambam and their school there. And so wrote Rabbeinu Yerucham, nesiv 1 chelek 7, regarding admission — see there — that even though Rav Ashi was a mumcheh, it only helps with three. And so wrote the Ritva in the second perek of Kesubos in the name of his teacher, and agreed with him, and I brought it below in siman 46 se'if 4 seif katan 8. And so wrote the Maharshal explicitly in perek HaGozel Basra siman 11, that [a single mumcheh helps] specifically regarding judging and the annulment of vows and the like, but regarding kiyum and odisa, in every place that requires a beis din there is no distinction — even the Reish Galusa, or the singular [authority] of his generation [it does not help] — see there.
